analysis:
This PR is a docs-only change to docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md: it adds a 'The cluster waitlist' section after base line ~48 (head lines 49-75). The supplied units are BASE text at lines 449-1312, which is unchanged context far from the changed range, so I could not see the head text directly. I judged the added section from the patch excerpt only. It documents `darkbloom waitlist cluster`, an account-level waitlist with manual approval. It says `darkbloom cluster` checks the waitlist before a new pair that serves through Darkbloom, that `darkbloom cluster local` needs no approval and no coordinator contact, and that already-paired Macs are never asked.

Security view: no code, key custody, attestation, encryption or authorization behavior changes. The doc says the waitlist sends nothing about the Macs, only the account. That is a data-minimization claim I cannot verify here against the CLI or coordinator implementation. The doc says the waitlist is an approval gate for public cluster serving. It does not replace the existing gates, namely cluster approvals, parity qualification, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052, T-053) and coordinator routing. The base text still says the coordinator's parity qualification decides each public placement, and the new section does not contradict that.

Open integration questions: (1) whether the new `darkbloom waitlist` CLI and its backend endpoint are implemented elsewhere in the PR, and how they authenticate and authorize (provider token, A-008), and whether they leak machine identifiers (T-058). (2) Whether the 'already-paired Macs never asked' grandfathering is enforced by the coordinator or only by the client, since a client-only check would not be a security control. I found no concrete regression in the supplied evidence.
